directAnswer: Windows Update may be stuck due to corrupted files, insufficient disk space, or network issues. Troubleshooting these areas can help resolve the problem.
summary: If Windows Update is not progressing, it could be due to various factors including system errors or connectivity issues. Follow the steps below to troubleshoot.

sections.heading: Common Causes of Windows Update Issues
sections.body: Windows Update can get stuck for several reasons, including corrupted update files, lack of disk space, or issues with the Windows Update service itself.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting Steps
sections.body: Follow these steps to troubleshoot and potentially resolve the issue with Windows Update.

steps.title: Check Disk Space
steps.detail: Ensure that you have enough free disk space on your system drive. Windows updates require sufficient space to download and install.

steps.title: Restart Windows Update Service
steps.detail: Open the Run dialog (Win + R), type 'services.msc', find 'Windows Update', right-click and select 'Restart'.

steps.title: Run Windows Update Troubleshooter
steps.detail: Go to Settings > Update & Security > Troubleshoot > Additional troubleshooters > Windows Update and run the troubleshooter.

steps.title: Clear Update Cache
steps.detail: Stop the Windows Update service, navigate to C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution\Download, delete all files, and then restart the service.

faqs.question: What should I do if Windows Update fails with an error code?
faqs.answer: Look up the specific error code on Microsoft's support site for tailored troubleshooting steps.

faqs.question: Can I manually download updates?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can manually download updates from the Microsoft Update Catalog website if automatic updates are not working.

faqs.question: How long should Windows Update take?
faqs.answer: While it varies, updates typically take anywhere from a few minutes to a couple of hours, depending on the size and your system's performance.

caveats: Some steps may vary slightly depending on your version of Windows (e.g., Windows 10 vs. Windows 11).
